# What each hypervisor supports

Generated from each provider's capability declaration -- the same one the validator and the translator read, so what is listed here is what vmctl will accept. Each provider states where its numbers came from; that line is the most important one in this file, because a measured limit and a remembered one look identical in a table.

Ask a specific host directly with `vmctl -p <provider> capabilities`, which also probes what only the machine can answer (bridges, machine types).

## libvirt

**Measured on:** probed on libvirt 11.10.0 / QEMU 10.1.0, machine q35; see tests/fixtures/libvirt_attach_matrix.json.

### Disk formats

| Format | Create | Attach | Extensions |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parallels` | - | - | hdd |
| `qcow2` (native) | yes | yes | qcow2 |
| `qed` | - | - | qed |
| `raw` | yes | yes | raw, img |
| `vdi` | - | yes | vdi |
| `vhd` | - | yes | vhd, vpc |
| `vhdx` | - | yes | vhdx |
| `vmdk` | - | yes | vmdk |

### Buses, and what attaches to them

| Bus | disk | cdrom | floppy | Ports | Bootable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `floppy` (native for floppy) | - | - | yes | 1-2 | yes |
| `sata` (native for cdrom) | yes | yes | - | 1-6 | yes |
| `scsi` | - | - | - | 1-256 | yes |
| `usb` | yes | yes | - | 1-8 | - |
| `virtio-blk` | yes | - | - | 1-256 | yes |
| `virtio-scsi` (native for disk) | yes | yes | - | 1-256 | yes |

### The rest

| | |
|---|---|
| CPUs | up to 240 |
| Memory | up to 4194304 MB |
| Devices | up to 256 |
| Network adapters | up to 8 |
| Firmware | `bios` (native), `efi` (read-write), `efi32` (unsupported), `efi64` (read-write) |
| Network modes | `nat`, `bridged`, `hostonly`, `internal` |
| Network cards | `e1000`, `e1000e`, `rtl8139`, `virtio` |
| CPU topology | yes |
| Machine types | q35, pc, pc-i440fx-rhel7.6.0, pc-q35-rhel7.6.0, pc-q35-rhel8.0.0, pc-q35-rhel8.1.0 |
| TPM | yes |
| Snapshots | yes, on `qcow2`; descriptions yes |
| NAT port forwards | yes |
